## Levels of AI-assisted development

| Level | Developer | AI  |
|---|---|---|
| Autocomplete | Current code | Predicting the next code |
| Conversational assistance | A question + selected context | Explaining or proposing an edit |
| Agentic coding | A goal | Planning, searching, editing, running |
| Agentic engineering | A goal + engineered environment | Executing within instructions, workflows, tools, validation |

# LLM fundametals

## Tokens
LLMs do not process text as whole sentences. A **tokenizer** splits it into tokens: words, parts of words, punctuation, or whitespace.

![](images/diagrams/tokens.svg){fig-alt="The sentence Agentic developers refactor code split into tokens, including word fragments, spaces, and punctuation" width="100%" fig-align="center"}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
As a rough rule of thumb for English: **1 token ≈ ¾ of a word**. The exact split depends on the tokenizer.
:::

## Autoregressive generation
<!-- Explain how LLMs generate text autoregressively, predicting the next token based on the previous tokens. Include a diagram showing the process of generating a sequence of tokens step by step. -->

An LLM generates one token at a time. Each chosen token is appended to the context before the model predicts again.

![](images/diagrams/autoregressive-generation.svg){fig-alt="Three steps of autoregressive generation, with each predicted token appended before the next prediction" width="100%" fig-align="center"}

::: {.fragment}
The model is not planning a complete sentence and revealing it—it is repeatedly answering: **“What token should come next?”**
:::
